title: Piercing Statue Solo #029 (데미스탯 · P25 집중형 · 목재(wenge) · 경계 겨드랑이 V자 · 체형 giant hourglass frame flaring · 트윈테일 · 애쉬그레이 · 메이크업 구풍 · 금속 금 · 재질 wenge · 쥬얼리 반지·헤어 장식·목걸이 JQ5 · 귀 보이기)
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, demi statue portrait. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips a little further below the middle of her thighs, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her thighs, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Chinese woman — porcelain-pale skin, slender upswept willow-leaf brows, a fine red floral huadian mark painted on the forehead, softly flushed rosy cheeks, an upswept eyeliner tail, large eyes with bright real catchlights, a small vivid red lip, a serene expression, cool ash-grey hair styled in twin-tail. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. Her neck, collarbones, shoulders and the upper chest above the line carry the same real living skin as her face: visible pores and fine skin grain, a soft sheen of natural skin oils on the highest planes, faint fine peach-fuzz hairs catching the rim light, gentle tonal variation with a natural warm flush, and the fine natural creases of a real neck — never airbrushed, never smooth like plastic. Like any real person she is slightly asymmetrical: a few small natural beauty marks and freckles scattered unevenly, one side of her neck and shoulder very slightly warmer and more freckled than the other.

Piercings: All twenty-five piercings gather mostly on the left side of her face, and the right side stays almost bare: on the left ear eight oversized pieces — a huge yellow-gold bar hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulder, a wide yellow-gold ear cuff, three smaller yellow-gold rings, two thick yellow-gold bars and a small yellow-gold stud up to the top; one small yellow-gold stud sits in the right ear; four thin yellow-gold bars pass through the outer half of the left eyebrow; two small yellow-gold rings pass through the left nostril and a thick yellow-gold septum ring hangs below the nose; a yellow-gold hoop passes through the left edge of the lower lip with a yellow-gold snake-bite ring beside it and a small yellow-gold ring at the left edge of the upper lip; a yellow-gold Medusa stud sits above the lips; a yellow-gold labret stud and a small yellow-gold ring sit on the chin; three small yellow-gold studs run along the left jaw. Each piece carries small mixed gemstones (diamond, pearl, opal, amethyst, ruby and sapphire) set into alternating pieces. All jewelry is real yellow gold, sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Jewelry: besides the piercings she wears well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of mixed-metal rings on her fingers; well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of mixed-metal hair ornaments set in her hair; well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of mixed-metal necklaces and chains resting on her neck, collarbones and upper chest, all of it real, sitting on and over the material of her body and her real neck and hair without covering her eyes, her face or her piercings.

Physique: A giant hourglass frame flaring at both ends — broad shoulders, a colossal chest projecting past them, a big round belly, hips as broad as the shoulders, both thighs clearly separate and individually shaped.

Body: Below the V-shaped line described in the boundary, her whole body — both arms from the shoulder joint down, hands, chest, belly, hips and both distinct thighs — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically made of one solid opaque wood, solid dark wenge wood, a deep near-black wood finely striped with narrow gold-tan pinstripes running through it, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, carved as one solid sculpted mass like a statue, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same material. A little further below the middle of her thighs, each thigh individually curves inward and rounds off into its own smooth, deeply polished tip — the two thighs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging, fusing or tapering into a single base — no calves, no feet, nothing continues below either tip — the material simply reaching its natural end on each leg, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Material: everything below that V-shaped line is a completely opaque solid that no light passes through, while her real face, ears, neck, collarbones, shoulders and upper chest are living flesh. The body blocks the backdrop's glow entirely, its surface catching the light with a hard, honest sheen and soft contact shadows, so it is unmistakable that the body itself is carved from the material.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs from under each arm up across the front of each shoulder and dips in a shallow V to the centre of her upper chest — real skin above it (her face, neck, collarbones, shoulders and upper chest), material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded tip is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along that V-shaped line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a warm rose pink on one side and a soft cream on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, body angled 45 degrees, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right hand gently tucking a lock of hair back behind her right ear so the ear and its piercings show clearly, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: the glowing backdrop frames her whole silhouette from behind, a warm rose pink on one side and a soft cream on the other, while her opaque body blocks it completely. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears, and a thin cool rim light traces her whole figure so the carved surface of the material reads clearly. Only her face, ears, neck, shoulders and upper chest read as real skin. Shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
